channel_schema_note: the first Tier-2 slice (2026-09-13): a channel is base_radians + sign * cos(ageInTicks * frequency_radians_per_age_tick * wingspeed) * (float) PI * pi_scale [* limbSwingAmount] on ONE axis (x / y / z) of each listed bone, evaluated in the compiled float chain and order (the phase's two multiplies left to right, the base added last); wingspeed defaults to 1.0 (the Beaver's ANIM_SPEED), base_radians to 0; a key of the transcription is the delta from the bone's bind rotation on that axis (KeyframeLeg / tools/keyframe_clip.py)

models.face_order_note: the second Tier-2 slice (2026-09-13): this rig carries zero-thickness cubes (the two wings, 0 x 6 x 2, mirrored, rotated about Z at bind), each drawing its two coplanar faces without culling; where the two faces carry different texels the z-fight winner is the face emitted last (LEQUAL in-game; the harness's rasteriser: first) - and for a .mirror()ed cube flat in X the classic emits the +X-normal face before the -X one (Polygon.<init> negates the X normal of the WEST slot) while GeckoLib's buildQuads emits WEST (-X) before EAST (+X), so the candidate showed the OTHER face: run 1 of the chain refused the Cloud Shark at bind (changed 1.6 percent, contested 2.56 percent, every changed pixel on the three fins). The FaceOrder contract's open item for a cutout rig (a zero-thickness box, FaceOrder.java) - met by declaring the classic order here exactly as the PurplePower does; the seam permutes every cube's quads into it and the draw-order leg compares the per-quad normal sequences of both renderers on every capture; the descriptor requires the key (a re-exported pack that drops it gets one WARN)
